subject: URGENT: production latency surge + error spike — likely prefix-cache thrash
messages:
From: Amit Desai <amit@signalcloud.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, support@redwood.com
Cc: Vikram Rao <vikram@signalcloud.com>, CloudOps <cloudops@signalcloud.com>
Date: 2028-04-16T21:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden latency and 5xx spike after cache parameter change

Marcus —

We're seeing a severe production impact after the change your team rolled earlier today (prefix-cache window reduced from 600s -> 60s). Latency p95 jumped from ~120ms to >1.2s and error rate spiked to ~6% across our high-throughput routes. Throughput is effectively capped compared to baseline. We rolled back the client-side prefilling, but the platform behavior persists.

Attached is a sample of the request/response traces and a small heap of gzipped logs (signal_perf_dump_20280417.json).

This is on our largest tenant: many requests are hitting hot prefixes for user profiles. We suspect some kind of cache thrash or head-of-line blocking at the KV layer — requests are queuing on hot keys, and downstream batching seems to be accumulating and timing out.

We need an immediate remediation plan and ETA. Our customers are experiencing rate-limited feature failures.

— Amit
Amit Desai
Director, Cloud Reliability
SignalCloud


From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Amit Desai <amit@signalcloud.com>
Date: 2028-04-16T21:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency and 5xx spike after cache parameter change

Laura / Tessa / Jonas —

Amit flagged this to me. Thanks for the quick heads-up and the perf dump. I'm escalating to ops + eng leadership. Initial read: the prefix-cache TTL reduction could have reduced cache hit amplification, but for hot prefixes it may be forcing more frequent recalc/eviction cycles and exposing a KV lock hotspot. That can cause HOL blocking inside the prefetch/batching layer and cascading timeouts.

Immediate asks:
- Tessa: can you check the live KV eviction stats and prefix eviction rate on the SignalCloud tenant? (eta 15m)
- Jonas: confirm whether the recent kernel selection change this week allowed continuous batching windows to grow beyond SLOs for short sequences (eta 20m)
- Laura: prepare an exec note for SignalCloud (short, clear remedies + ETA). Keep it factual; do not promise a timeline longer than we can meet.

I'm copying Amit so they can see we're on it. If we confirm KV thrash, prioritized mitigations are: bump prefix-cache back for affected tenant, enable hot-key bypass to a dedicated hot lane, and throttle aggressive prefetchers.

Marcus
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Desai <amit@signalcloud.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-16T21:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency and 5xx spike after cache parameter change

Marcus / team — quick findings from the first 20m:

- KV eviction rate for SignalCloud tenant spiked ~22x post-change; prefix eviction churn is concentrated on ~12 prefixes (top 0.01% of keys).
- Batch sizes on the inference worker increased (avg batch size +40%) because many small requests were queued behind hot-key processing; that increased end-to-end tail latency.
- We observed repeated lock waits on the prefix slot leading to HOl (head-of-line) queueing; several worker threads show >200ms lock hold times.

Action taken (live):
- Temporarily reverted prefix-cache window to 600s for SignalCloud only (started at 21:42).
- Enabled hot-key bypass -> pinned hot prefixes to a dedicated lane (experimental).
- Dropped aggressive prefetchers for the tenant.

Immediate effect: p95 latency moving from ~1.2s -> ~350ms in the last 6 minutes; 5xx rate falling but still elevated (~1.2%).

Next steps:
- Jonas to validate whether the recent batch-lane selector change increased lock contention (logs & flamegraphs).
- I'll keep rolling safe mitigations; need to coordinate with SignalCloud to keep their client prefilling off for 1h.

Tessa
Product Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Desai <amit@signalcloud.com>
Date: 2028-04-16T22:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency and 5xx spike after cache parameter change

Quick diagnostic summary:

- The runtime's batching lane selector introduced a subtle change in the last rollout: we loosened the lane threshold to favor larger batches for throughput. Under normal distributions that improves cost, but with the SignalCloud prefix distribution (a very heavy skew), it allowed hot-key candidates to occupy larger batches and hold KV cache locks longer. That amplified contention and produced HOL blocking across shards.
- Also found a regression in the prefix-lock code where backoff jitter was effectively disabled for >5s windows (PR #4871). That explains the long lock hold/resend behavior.

Remediations implemented:
- Reverted the lane selector threshold for the SignalCloud region (applied 21:48).
- Reinstated exponential jitter on prefix lock backoff (hotfix deployed 22:03).
- Added temporary per-tenant hot-key rate-limiting and a guard that prevents batching with >X concurrent hot prefixes.

Impact: error rate dropped from 6% -> 0.9% over 30m; p95 currently trending ~220-300ms, still not at baseline.

I'll open a postmortem and a targeted test in staging to validate lane selector behavior under skewed prefix distributions.

— Jonas
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Amit Desai <amit@signalcloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-17T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency and 5xx spike after cache parameter change

Amit / Vikram —

Update and commitments: thanks for your patience. High level: the root cause was an interaction between the prefix-cache TTL change and a recently loosened batching lane selector. For your tenant's skewed prefix distribution this produced eviction churn, KV lock hold-lengths, and HOL blocking that cascaded into increased batch sizes and timeouts.

What we did (already live):
- Rolled back prefix-cache TTL for SignalCloud to the prior setting.
- Pinned top hot prefixes to a dedicated hot-lane to avoid interfering with normal batching.
- Re-enabled exponential backoff/jitter on prefix lock acquisition; reduced lock hold duration in runtime hot path.
- Throttled prefetching for your tenant for the next 60 minutes while we monitor.

Immediate impact: error rate back within 1% and p95 down to ~230ms; we'll aim to reach baseline within 4 hours and follow with a full RCA.

Next steps / owner map: 
- Redwood (Jonas/Tessa): full postmortem + tests to prevent regressions (deliverable EOD + link to RCA).
- Redwood (Laura): exec note and customer-facing timeline (live in 30m).
- SignalCloud (Amit): please keep client prefilling disabled for 1 hour and confirm if you want us to create a dedicated reserved hot-lane longer term.

I've attached a short executive slide pack with the current impact metrics (slo_escalation_slides.pdf) and the raw perf dump we analyzed. We'll open JIRA-OPS-2498 for the follow-up items.

Marcus
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
